Chinese humanoid robots broke records set by humans, including Usain Bolt's 100m sprint world record, on the opening day of the Olympics-like World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing on Saturday. More than 2,000 humanoid robots were participating in the event, organisers said. In a 100-metre sprint, a humanoid robot achieved a result of 9.39 seconds, beating the human record of 9.58 seconds set by Jamaican athlete Bolt in 2009. In a standing high jump, a humanoid robot was able to reach 2.88m, well above the 0.95m best result by a humanoid in last year’s first edition of the games. It surpassed the human high jump record of 2.45m set by Cuba’s Javier Sotomayor in 1993. The five-day games, now in their second year, are a spectacle demonstrating China’s rapid progress in advanced robotics as the technology race with the US heats up. There are 51 events and more than 1,000 competitions taking place, including running, table tennis and football. For more news, visit @sbsnews_au (link in bio).

Rekbot, el robot humanoide de 1.80 metros desarrollado por la empresa de robótica REK Robotics combina realidad virtual, robótica y entretenimiento en una experiencia de combate. Inspirado en el T-800 de Terminator y equipado con movimientos de gran potencia, el humanoide forma parte de una propuesta en la que los participantes compiten primero en un videojuego de realidad virtual. En este video, un robot masilla las juntas de los paneles de yeso, demostrando precisión y eficiencia en cada movimiento, sea real o animado, nos invita a reflexionar:  En el futuro, los robots realizarán muchos de los trabajos difíciles, repetitivos y peligrosos que hoy enfrentamos. Pero hay algo que las máquinas no pueden replicar: nuestra creatividad, nuestra ética y nuestra capacidad de soñar.Los robots serán nuestros aliados, facilitando nuestras labores y permitiéndonos enfocarnos en lo que realmente importa. Seremos nosotros quienes diseñemos, innovemos y tomemos decisiones basadas en valores humanos.Mientras los robots se encargan del trabajo arduo, nosotros, los humanos, seguiremos liderando con imaginación y corazón. Porque aunque la tecnología avance, la chispa de la humanidad nunca será reemplazada.  ¿Qué opinas sobre el futuro de la tecnología en la construcción? artist and automata maker Amedeo Capelli, known as Stoccafisso Design, creates playful mechanical sculptures from wood, wire and simple mechanisms. In his recent shrimp automata, a handmade crustacean comes to life through a system of wooden gears, cams, rods and rotating parts hidden beneath the stage. Turning the crank transfers motion through the mechanism, making the shrimp’s body and limbs move in an exaggerated, almost theatrical way. Capelli’s work combines traditional automata-making, kinetic sculpture and humor. Instead of hiding the mechanics, he often leaves them visible, allowing us to understand how a simple rotation can be transformed into surprisingly complex movement. #shrimp #art #artist #niche #weird

A humanoid robot was blasted in the chest and still stayed on its feet. This viral video appears to show two armored humanoid robots being struck by rounds claimed to be from a 20 mm cannon. Sparks, smoke, and debris fly as the machines absorb the impacts, yet neither one collapses. If authentic, it could offer a disturbing glimpse into the future of military robotics: machines designed not only to walk and work, but also to survive dangerous combat environments. However, the video does not identify the manufacturer, testing organization, or location, and the claims have not been independently verified. Impressive engineering, clever visual effects, or an early look at future warfare? Would robots like these make soldiers safer, or make warfare even more dangerous?
